name: Shoko
description:
A Jellyfin plugin to integrate [Jellyfin](https://jellyfin.org/docs/) with [Shoko Server](https://shokoanime.com/downloads/shoko-server/).
## Read this before installing
**This plugin requires that you have already set up and are using Shoko Server**, and that the files you intend to include in Jellyfin are **indexed** (and optionally managed) by Shoko Server. **Otherwise, the plugin won't be able to provide metadata for your files**, since there is no metadata to find for them.
overview: Manage your anime from Jellyfin using metadata from Shoko

versions.changelog: `repo`: **Move http extensions dll from own to shared**.

`chore`: **Await in async task**.

`repo`: **Refine build process**:

- Updated the .csproj project file to not hard code copying of the DLLs, and instead which DLLs to copy based on the project references

- Updated the .csproj project file to conditionally load a local jellyfin project or the nuget package depending on if said local project is available or not.

- Updated the JPRM build process to dynamically include the DLLs in the .csproj project file instead of hard coding them in the build configuration file.

`fix`: **Always display save button for library settings section**.

`fix`: **Add missing library id check when adding a new path**.

`feat`: **Add per-library media folder management**:

Allows adding and removing media folders per library configuration.
Removes the older approach of resetting all mappings and settings,
as this is now handled individually per media folder.

`chore`: **Change data option selector to use double quotes**.

`refactor`: **Rework library configuration**:

- Reworked how the library configurations are stored, finally separating the library configuration from the media folder configurations. This has simplified the configuration for libraries, so we don't store `n` copies of the settings that applies to all the media folders.

- We now automatically remove the media folders from the library and only store them in the configuration if the VFS is enabled. This will simplify some of the plugin internals, and also speed up the library validation as Jellyfin doesn't need to "validate" the contents within them before ignoring it all and instead use the VFS. Libraries not using the VFS should be unaffected by this change. In fact, we'll add them back to the library and remove the VFS root if you disable the VFS.

- The real-time monitoring portions of the plugin has now been simplified for VFS based libraries as we're now not obstructing Jellyfin from seeing into the other media folders attached to the library — since they're simply not attached anymore! 😌
